영입 조건을 달성한 뒤에는 그 비스티에게 줄 유니폼이 있어야 해요. 유니폼은 비스티볼 센터에서 살 수 있어요. 비싼 유니폼일수록 높은 레벨의 비스티를 영입할 수 있어요!

[scaleStack,2]WELCOME![scaleStack,.75]\nRutile Nature Preserve

The rock garden before you is a scale model of the nature preserve,| which you can enter just ahead.

This nature preserve is a vital Beastie habitat and has been maintained for generations with minimal human intervention. We thank you for treating the land respectfully.

Throughout the preserve you'll find many rarely-seen Beasties. They are safe to observe and will tend to ignore humans. However, take care when picking any black and white ball mushrooms scattered around! Some Beasties might take this as an invitation to play Beastieball. Only trained coaches should engage in Beastieball activites.
Sign and garden maintained by the Rutile Town Board
[scaleStack,1.5]WOW: A Rare Sight!

Sprecko (pictured here) are one of the rarest Beasties you might find in the preserve. That's because they are an endangered species!\n\nSprecko have sticky bodies and pick up forest detritus as they move about. Different Sprecko prefer to collect different berries; you can tell which is their favorite by which is stuck to their tail. Most berries they collect are for eating, but they are also known to plant some, making them nature's own little gardeners!
Remember to pick up after yourself!
[scaleStack,.75]The Beautiful...\n[scaleStack,2]Crown Farms!

Crown Farms is a shining symbol of the Beastieball League's commitment to environmental protection.

Every day, coaches both Ranked and unranked play Beastieball with regulation rubber balls produced by the League. These farms are the first step in the production of those balls!

For many years, the League manufactured artificial rubber in factories that generated toxic wastewater. Eventually it was uncovered that this had lasting and harmful environmental impact. In response, the League shut down its rubber factories. This land was then developed so that rubber could be harvested organically and in perfect communion with nature.
Property of the Beastieball League
[scaleStack,1.5]The Process of Rubber Farming

Rubber trees, when cut, secrete a white liquid we call "Rubber milk." This milk is collected in cups and then processed, solidifed, and dried into sheets that are ready for use in manufacturing.\n\nSheets from this farm are transported to Geo City, where they are assembled into the Beastie balls we all know and love!
[scaleStack,1.4]Neptune\nStadium

Perhaps the most ambitious construction project ever attempted by humanity, Neptune Stadium survives as only a shadow of its beautiful vision.

This would have been the home of the Beastieball League, taking the place of Crown Stadium. This stadium could float on the sea and even travel from city to city, making the Crown Series a travelling worldwide event.

Tragically, ocean Beasties perceived it as a threat, and its construction was regularly disrupted by massive Tortanchors. Eventually construction was abandoned due to safety concerns. It has since drifted across the Chroma Sea and settled at the edge of this coral reef, where it is expected to remain for the foreseeable future.
Property of the Beastieball League
[scaleStack,1.5]Life in the Stadium

The Stadium would have doubled as a sports arena and a luxury cruise line. Its design prioritized beauty and comfort and was packed with state of the art amenities. Space onboard was reserved for high-end restaurants, swimming pools, theaters and social event spaces.\n\nWhile we'll never get to see the highest competition on the high seas, the League is committed to building newer and better stadiums in the future!
WARNING: Do NOT attempt to board or explore the stadium. Violators will be charged fines up to $25,000.
